title: A 1Tb 3b/cell 3D-Flash Memory with a 29%-Improved-Energy-Efficiency Read Operation and 4.8Gb/s Power-Isolated Low-Tapped-Termination I/Os
problem: 3D Flash memory for AI applications requires high-speed I/O and energy-efficient reads; reducing circuit overhang from the memory array (in CMOS-bonded-array or CMOS-under-array designs) limits chip area, while energy efficiency is critical for large-scale deployments.
motivation: AI workloads demand dense 3D Flash with high-speed I/O and low energy consumption; balancing area efficiency (small overhang) with energy efficiency is essential for practical deployment.
method: The chip stores 1 terabyte using 3D Flash memory (vertically stacked silicon), with each cell holding 3 bits. It cuts read power consumption by 29% through small-voltage-swing word-line control (applying smaller electrical pulses to activate memory rows instead of large ones, which wastes less energy). Data moves at 4.8 gigabits per second via power-isolated low-tapped-termination I/Os (data connections that keep support circuits tightly bundled), minimizing the extra area needed beyond the memory array.
key_novelty: The key innovation is reducing the voltage pulse for memory row activation (small-voltage-swing word-line control), achieving 29% lower read energy while keeping support circuits tightly integrated with the memory in 3D stacking.
